forecast-period.text: A high pressure ridge builds across much of SA, as a cold front slips across southern coasts late today into early Tuesday. A high pressure system will then move across waters to the south throughout the week to be centred over Victoria by Thursday. A low pressure trough in the interior of WA may extend into far western parts at times before weakening by late Tuesday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning fog about parts of the Agricultural Areas and West Coast. Showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far northwest. Isolated showers developing about southern coastal districts during the afternoon and extending over the remainder of the Southern Agricultural Area during the night. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast, tending near average elsewhere. Southwest to southeasterly winds, freshening about the coast during the night.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far northwest, with isolated light showers possible about parts of the Agricultural Areas and Mid North district clearing by the afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh about the coast and central and northern inland parts.
Possible patchy morning frost about the Flinders Ranges. Dry and mostly sunny. Maximum temperatures below average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh and gusty in the northeast.

text.p: Possible patchy morning frost on and east of the ranges, with patchy fog also possible in the southeast. Dry and mostly sunny. Maximum temperatures below average, tending above average in the southwest. East to northeasterly winds, fresh and gusty in the northeast during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: less than 2 mm about the Northern Agricultural Area, reaching up to 2 to 5 mm about the Southern Agricultural Area and 5 to 10 mm about southern coasts, ranges and the South East. Local heavier falls are possible between 5 to 15 mm. 5 to 15 mm possible in the far west, with local heavier falls between 20 to 40 mm possible.
